rows.notes: odai never builds llama.cpp: it speaks the protocol on both sides, as a client through the llama-server backend and as a server through the shim. Only tools/server/ is tracked — the route table in server.cpp, the endpoint reference in README.md, and the test suite the conformance runner drives. A commit anywhere else in llama.cpp (ggml, the CLI, the model code) is not drift for us. Upgrade policy is locked because llama.cpp tags a b<build> release every few hours with no semver: adopting a pin is a deliberate re-verification, not an auto-bump.

The shim answers the same routes llama-server answers, so llama-server's own pytest suite is the spec. Drift here means an upstream test changed: re-run `pnpm run test:conformance` and either implement the new behavior or move the case into .config/repo/llama-cpp-server.allowlist with a reason. The runner already fails on an allowlisted case that starts passing and on an allowlist id the run never reports, so the two directions of drift are both covered.
